claims.text: Adding lanthanum will reduce phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The target alloy may have either an FCC or BCC crystal structure.
The intervention is the addition of 1–2 at.% lanthanum.
The proposed effect applies to polycrystalline alloys with grain size greater than 1 micrometer.
The proposed effect applies between 300 and 1000 K.
The large atomic radius of lanthanum causes lattice distortions in the alloy.
Lanthanum-induced lattice distortions increase phonon scattering.
Phonon scattering by lattice distortions reduces the phonon mean free path.
The reduced phonon mean free path decreases thermal conductivity.
Adding 1–2 at.% lanthanum will reduce phonon thermal conductivity by 10–20% relative to the untreated alloy.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction may depend on alloy composition and processing history.
Lanthanum addition may affect strength or corrosion resistance.
Failure to observe at least a 5% thermal-conductivity reduction would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe lattice distortions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as having the same composition as the treated alloy while also lacking the added lanthanum. These cannot both be literally true; the intended control presumably has the same non-lanthanum composition and processing history.

The predicted reduction is 10–20%, but the hypothesis is falsified only below 5%. An observed reduction between 5% and 10% would contradict the stated quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
